brief: Zero Hedge argues the AI bull case contains an internal cash flow inconsistency. It opens by noting the BIS warned this summer about unprecedented circular financing inside the AI ecosystem, with off balance sheet AI financing arrangements having grown to $3.1 trillion. The core argument, credited to Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok, is that because Wall Street analysts work in sector silos, their aggregate forecasts do not add up. Tech sector analysts expect operating cash flow to more than double to roughly $2.4 trillion by 2028. Hyperscalers are forecast to generate over $120 billion in free cash flow by 2030, even though maintenance capex alone on the data center buildout will reach $920 billion within a few years, and token prices have fallen as users shift to Chinese open weight models. Analysts covering tech's customer sectors forecast much smaller cash flow gains, so either those customers will spend far more than expected or tech's forecasts are too optimistic. The piece concludes the latter, and that AI's ubiquitous buzz has so far produced no measurable spending or productivity gains.
